title: Working Remotely from Türkiye: Digital Nomad Visa, Work Permissions, Tax & Social Security
excerpt: What remote workers need to know about Türkiye’s Digital Nomad route, Turkish work permissions, tax residence, employer approval, and social security.
bodyHtml:
Working from Türkiye can be straightforward for a short stay, but immigration status, the right to work, tax, employer policy, and social security are separate questions. A visa-free entry or residence permit is not a blanket authorisation to work in Türkiye.

This guide is practical information, not legal or tax advice. Rules and consular requirements can change, so confirm your personal case with the relevant authority and a qualified adviser before relocating.

The Digital Nomad route

Türkiye has a Digital Nomad programme for eligible remote workers. The official Digital Nomads portal currently lists requirements including:

  • Age 21–55

  • A university degree

  • A passport valid for at least six months

  • A contract with a company outside Türkiye, or business activity with clients outside Türkiye

  • Monthly income of at least USD 3,000, or USD 36,000 annually

  • Citizenship of an eligible country

Applicants first apply for a Digital Nomad Identification Certificate through the official portal. With that certificate, they follow the visa process through the relevant Turkish consulate or visa application centre.

Do not rely on an old country list or a blog post. Eligibility, document requirements, fees, appointment availability, and the process can vary by consulate. Check the official Digital Nomads portal and the Turkish mission responsible for your place of residence.

A certificate, visa, residence permit, and work permission are different

It is useful to separate the stages:

Digital Nomad certificate → visa application → possible residence-permit application

These are related, but they are not interchangeable.

YİMER states that successful Digital Nomad applicants may apply through e-İkamet for a six-month short-term residence permit for tourism purposes during the visa period. An application is not an approval, and a residence permit alone does not generally create the right to take local employment.

Can you work for a Turkish employer or client?

Treat this as a separate question from remote work for a foreign employer or overseas clients.

Foreigners working in Türkiye generally need a work permit or a formal work-permit exemption unless a specific legal exception applies. Turkish employment, regular work for Turkish clients, or locally structured self-employment can create labour, immigration, tax, and social-security obligations.

A work-permit exemption is an official document issued through the Ministry’s process. It is not something to assume based on a tourist entry, Digital Nomad status, or short-term residence permit.

If your work involves a Turkish employer, Turkish clients, or a Turkish entity, get tailored advice before beginning work.

Get written employer approval

Even if your immigration position is in order, your employer may have its own restrictions on where you can work.

Longer-term work from Türkiye can raise questions for a foreign employer around payroll, corporate tax, permanent establishment, data security, insurance, client contracts, and social security. These outcomes depend on the facts, but they should not be discovered after you have moved.

Before relocating, ask your employer for written approval and confirm:

  • Whether Türkiye is an approved work location

  • How long you may work there

  • Whether your role, client access, or data access is restricted

  • Whether payroll, tax, or insurance arrangements need to change

Tax residence: the six-month rule is only a starting point

Under Türkiye’s general tax framework, someone may be treated as tax resident if they are domiciled in Türkiye or stay continuously in Türkiye for more than six months in a calendar year. Temporary absences do not necessarily interrupt that period.

There are exceptions for some people in Türkiye temporarily for work, business, study, treatment, rest, or travel. Tax treaties and the details of your home, work, income, and personal ties can also affect the result.

Tax residents are generally taxed on worldwide income, subject to applicable exemptions and tax treaties. Non-residents may still have Turkish tax obligations on certain Turkish-source income.

Do not assume that being paid abroad, using a foreign bank account, or working for a foreign company automatically means there is no Turkish tax exposure.

The new foreign-income exemption

A new provision, effective for people treated as Turkish tax residents from 1 January 2026, can provide a 20-year Turkish income-tax exemption for certain foreign income and gains.

In broad terms, it is intended for individuals who became resident in Türkiye after having no Turkish domicile or tax liability during the previous three calendar years.

This is important, but it is not an automatic “remote-worker tax exemption.” Whether your salary, freelance income, dividends, or other income qualifies depends on how the income is classified and sourced, your individual history, and any applicable tax treaty. Obtain advice before relying on it.

Social security is separate from tax

Social-security coverage is not determined solely by your visa or tax residence. Türkiye has bilateral social-security agreements with 35 countries, but the result depends on the country, the agreement, your employment arrangement, and whether you remain covered in your home system.

If you are sent to Türkiye by a foreign employer, self-employed, or working remotely for an overseas company, check:

  • Whether a social-security agreement applies

  • Whether you need proof of continuing coverage in your home country

  • Whether Turkish contributions may be due

  • Whether your health insurance meets the requirements for your stay

Do this before relocating; health insurance, social security, and immigration documentation often overlap in practice.

A practical pre-flight checklist

Before working remotely from Türkiye, confirm:

  • Your entry route and permitted stay

  • Whether you qualify for the Digital Nomad route

  • The Turkish mission’s current document requirements

  • Written approval from your employer

  • Whether your work touches Turkish clients, entities, or employment

  • Your likely tax-residence position

  • Whether the foreign-income exemption may apply to your exact income

  • Your social-security and health-insurance coverage

  • Your plan for a residence permit if staying longer
